newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope writes to Netanyahu, Arafat on Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Pope writes to Netanyahu, Arafat on Mideast peace.

text.p: Pope John Paul has urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to put the stalled Mideast peace process back on track.

In two letters, dated June 16 and released on Thursday, the Pope expressed "deep worry" that the dialogue between Israelis and Palestinians was "practically at a standstill" and appealed to the two Mideast leaders to redouble their efforts.

"It must be admitted that the much hoped-for dialogue between the parties, and in particular between the government over which you preside and the leaders of the Palestinian people, is practically at a standstill," the Pope said in the letter to Netanyahu.

"The Israeli and Palestinian peoples are already shouldering a burden of suffering which is too heavy. This burden must not be increased, instead it deserves the utmost commitment to finding the paths of necessary and courageous compromises," the Pope told the Israeli leader.

In his letter to Arafat, the Pope spoke of a "de facto interruption of dialogue" and added: "My fear is that if this situation continues it will become increasingly difficult to revive the quest for the trust that is essential to every negotiation."

In both letters the Pontiff said that a Holy Land at peace would be a worthy way of welcoming the many pilgrims expected to visit the region for the start of the third millennium of Christianity in the year 2000.
